description: A person, without saying who; often used in questions and negative sentences.
questions: Did ____ leave a red umbrella on the bus? I would like to return it to its owner.
I knocked on every door, but I could not find ____ at home to answer my questions.

description: A thing, without saying what; often used in questions and negative sentences.
questions: Is there ____ in your bag that you need for the trip? Check before we leave.
The room was so dark that I could not see ____ at all, not even the chairs.

description: All the people in a group. It takes a singular verb: everyone is.
questions: All thirty pupils passed the test, so ____ in the class passed.
Every member of the team was present; ____ was ready to start the game.

description: All the things in a group. It takes a singular verb: everything is.
questions: I packed my shoes, coat, books and lunch. Now ____ on my packing list is in my suitcase.
Mum checked every item on the shopping list; she had bought ____ on it.

description: Not a single person. Write it as two words; it takes a singular verb: no one is.
questions: All the children had gone home, so ____ was left in the classroom.
The hall was empty. ____ was there to hear the announcement.

description: Not one or not any of a particular group of people or things; often followed by ‘of’.
questions: I offered three biscuits to my friends, but ____ of them wanted one.
There were five balloons, but ____ of them survived after they all burst.

description: Not a single thing. It is already negative, so avoid adding another negative to the same clause.
questions: The box was empty; there was ____ inside it.
I searched the drawer, but I found ____ in it because it was completely empty.

description: A person whose identity is unknown or not stated; often used in positive statements.
questions: ____ rang the doorbell, but I could not see who it was.
There is a person waiting outside the office, but I do not know who it is. ____ would like to speak to the teacher.

description: A thing whose identity is unknown or not stated; often used in positive statements.
questions: I heard a strange noise under the bed. ____ was moving there, but I could not tell what it was.
Mum has put a surprise in the parcel. I know there is ____ inside, but I do not know what it is.
